title: Align worker account sharing with confirmed login identities

owned: .orchestrator/config.json provider.account mapping for claude2 and codex2/codex2-1..4
.orchestrator/test_supervisor.py repo-config contract test that asserted claude/claude2 used isolated accounts
not_changing: logical agent identities, worker_slots, and per-agent max_parallel (claude=3, claude2=1, codex=2, codex2=2)
credential values, auth directories, model settings, or task owner/reviewer assignments
the primary shared-account caps claude1=3 and codex1=2
any grouping/adapter abstraction layer; sharing uses the existing provider.account field directly
composes_with: the operator-confirmed auth-file copy and byte-equality verification performed by root outside this repo

failure_reproduction.case: providers.claude2.account was "claude2" and providers.codex2 / codex2-1..4 .account were "codex2", each with their own entries in ready_dispatcher.max_concurrent_per_account, even though the operator confirmed Claude2 logs into the same Anthropic account/org as Claude, and Codex2 was deliberately given a byte-identical copy of Codex's login data.
failure_reproduction.prior_outcome: Capacity accounting treated claude/claude2 and codex/codex2 as fully independent accounts, understating that they draw against one shared provider-side quota.
failure_reproduction.regression: test_repo_claude_accounts_are_isolated_at_requested_capacities in .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py explicitly asserted providers.claude.account != providers.claude2.account, which is now false by design and had to be replaced.

implementation.config_change: providers.claude2.account, providers.codex2.account, and providers.codex2-1/-2/-3/-4.account now all read "claude1" / "codex1" respectively, matching the operator-confirmed shared login identity.
implementation.account_cap_cleanup: ready_dispatcher.max_concurrent_per_account no longer declares the now-unreferenced "claude2" (was 1) and "codex2" (was 2) keys; claude1=3, codex1=2, antigravity=4, antigravity2=4, copilot=0, and the global max_concurrent_workers=13 are unchanged.
implementation.identity_preservation: agents.claude2/codex2/codex2-1..4 keep their own display_name, provider, max_parallel, worker_slots, and dispatch_slot_for entries untouched, so logical identities and physical slots are unaffected; only the shared account they draw capacity from changed.
implementation.test_update: Replaced test_repo_claude_accounts_are_isolated_at_requested_capacities with test_repo_claude_and_codex_accounts_are_shared_at_confirmed_capacities, which asserts both members of each shared-account group resolve to the same account, keep their own individual dispatch capacity/slots, and that the shared account cap equals the confirmed primary cap (claude1=3, codex1=2); it also asserts the obsolete claude2/codex2 keys are absent from max_concurrent_per_account.

broader_nonpassing_observations.detail: Fails identically on the unmodified config.json/test_supervisor.py (verified by stashing this task's diff and re-running); assert_task_archive_root_binding rejects the fixture because the legacy-collision fixture leaves task_archive globals bound to another status root in this worktree environment. Not touched by this task's account-mapping change.

review_decision.note: Independently verify the confirmed shared-account mapping (claude2->claude1, codex2/codex2-1..4->codex1), the max_concurrent_per_account cleanup, that no credential/auth/model/assignment fields were touched, and the replacement repo-config contract test at the exact PR head.
